statement: An employer must pay CPF contributions for every employee who is a Singapore citizen or permanent resident employed under a contract of service and earning total wages of more than $50 per month; contributions are due on the last day of the calendar month, enforcement begins against employers who have not paid by the 14th of the following month, and the rate for employees aged 55 and below earning over $750 per month is 37% of wages from 1 January 2026 (17% employer, 20% employee).
caveat: Foreign employees are outside CPF entirely (work-pass rules apply instead), rates step down in the age bands above 55 and differ in an SPR's first two years, and a rate increase for senior employees lands 1 January 2027. The statutory source is the Central Provident Fund Act 1953 section 7 and its First Schedule.
